ai.description: This slender snake reaches 1.5m. It is olive-brown with a series of dark, diamond-shaped dorsal blotches and a distinct, dark post-ocular stripe. It features a broad head and large, vertical pupils.
ai.identificationRemarks: The *Boiga quincunciata* is best distinguished by its distinct, dark, diamond-shaped vertebral blotches that are separated by narrow, pale interspaces along the body.
ai.habitat: The Assamese Cat Snake inhabits dense, humid tropical evergreen and semi-evergreen forests, typically found at low to moderate elevations within the Indian subcontinent.
ai.behavior: The Assamese Cat Snake is primarily nocturnal and arboreal, often hunting for lizards and birds among tree branches under the cover of darkness.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Boiga quincunciata* is oviparous, laying clutches of 6–12 eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, with hatchlings appearing shortly thereafter.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Assamese Cat Snake occurs in Northeast India, primarily within the states of Assam and Arunachal Pradesh, inhabiting tropical forests at low to moderate elevations.
